member.name: T:Meziantou.Framework.Ntp.NtpClient
member.summary: An NTP client for querying NTP servers to retrieve accurate network time. Supports NTPv3 and NTPv4.
member.remarks: Responses are validated as described on , but they are never authenticated cryptographically. An attacker who can inject packets on the path to the server can still control the reported time.

member.remarks: A host name can resolve to several addresses, and each one gets this much time, so a query can take up to Timeout × addressCount overall. Use the cancellationToken of to bound the total duration.

member.name: P:Meziantou.Framework.Ntp.NtpClientOptions.ValidateResponse
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether responses are validated before being returned. Default is .

remarks.para: When enabled, a response is only accepted if its originate timestamp echoes the transmit timestamp of the request (RFC 5905 TEST2), its version is 3 or 4, its stratum is not 0 (Kiss-o'-Death), and the server does not report an alarm condition. Responses that fail are ignored and the client keeps waiting for a valid one until elapses.

The originate timestamp is what ties a reply to this specific request, so disabling this makes the client accept a forged reply from anyone who can guess its source port. Only turn it off to interoperate with a server known to be non-compliant, and do not use the result to make a security decision. This library never authenticates the server cryptographically: it implements neither NTS (RFC 8915) nor symmetric key authentication.

member.name: T:Meziantou.Framework.Ntp.NtpTimestamp
member.summary: Provides conversion between NTP 64-bit timestamps and . NTP timestamps consist of 32 bits for seconds since 1900-01-01 and 32 bits for fractional seconds.
member.remarks: The 32-bit seconds field wraps every 136 years, so it cannot by itself identify an instant. Following RFC 5905 section 6, a seconds value with the high bit set belongs to era 0 (1968-2036) and a value with the high bit clear belongs to era 1 (2036-2104). Instants outside that window cannot be represented and are rejected by rather than silently wrapping.
